population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 47M of ~265M US adults are currently on an incretin (17.8%), for any indication. Age check: 0.20×9 + 0.33×17.5 + 0.24×29 + 0.23×14.5 ≈ 17.9. Income thirds (12/18/23) average to about 17.7. The bottom third is held down by employer retreat and sits only as high as it does because of diabetes-coded coverage and gray-market product. Cycling arithmetic: ever 24% − current 17.8% = 6.2% of adults who used and are off now. Taking the parent's ~40% one-year restart rate and three years of churn, about 35% of current users are restarters (0.35×17.8 ≈ 6.2 pp), and about 20% of those currently off had already cycled once before (0.2×6.2 ≈ 1.2 pp), so (6.2+1.2)/24 ≈ 31% of ever-users have stopped and restarted at least once. About 16M adults have used and stopped; around 5M of them stopped because a coverage change, rather than a side effect, ended it. Payer mix of the 47M current users: diabetes- or cardiac-coded coverage across all payers ~20M; employer obesity coverage ~8M; Medicare obesity-only (Continuity Model) ~1.5M; Medicaid obesity ~1.5M; brand cash via TrumpRx/direct ~10M; gray market ~6M. These sum to 47M. Pediatric: ~0.7% of under-18s (~0.5M), almost all aged 12+. Upper-income skew persists. Under-12 use is still off-label and specialist-only. Most children with obesity are untreated; a much larger number live in households where a parent is on the drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ended Dec 2027. It was replaced from Jan 2028 by the CMS Medicare GLP-1 Continuity Model on the same terms (Medicare pays ~$245/month, beneficiary copay ~$50), with an adherence condition added. To keep coverage, a beneficiary needs ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered by refill data and ≥5% weight loss at 6 months; a lapse brings a 12-month re-enrollment lockout. About 1.5M obesity-only beneficiaries are enrolled. Spending: 1.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.4B/yr, in line with CBO's ≥$35B over 2026–2034 (~$4B/yr). Medicaid: 19 states cover obesity at the $245 rate for about 1.5M enrollees. Gross cost is 1.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $4.4B/yr, of which the federal share at a ~65% blended FMAP is ≈ $2.9B. Seven of those states attach the same adherence and refill conditions through waivers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 60+ generic semaglutide brands at ~$8–40/month. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and most of Southeast Asia have generics at roughly CAD 70–110 or local equivalents. Generic oral semaglutide is launching in India in 2028. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: Price follows the managed-decline path. TrumpRx and manufacturer direct prices: injectable semaglutide $199/month, Zepbound $249–299, orals (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) from $149. Retatrutide launched at $399 direct cash (list $1,299), the one premium exception to the $150–300 band. List prices are unchanged and almost nobody pays them. Employer coverage for weight management fell 60%→52% (2027)→44% (2028, Business Group on Health), with WTW at ~40%. Most remaining employer coverage requires a T2D, established CVD, OSA or MASH code, or a BMI ≥35 with comorbidity plus enrolment in a vendor lifestyle programme. Gray market: the FDA finalised the 503B exclusion (Sep 2027), and supply then moved to three channels. (1) Telehealth 'personal importation' of Indian and Turkish generics at $60–120/month. (2) 503A 'personalised dose' compounding that survives in court on patient-specific grounds. (3) 'Research peptide' retatrutide and cagrilintide sold 'not for human consumption' at $150–250/month. Together these serve about 6M people (~13% of users). New starts are now ~35% oral.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Feb 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema; approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity (semaglutide, Sep 2028)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: nicotine cessation in normal-weight smokers and vapers (off-label since the Sep 2028 approval)
alcohol reduction: RCT-supported, still unapproved; a phase 3 AUD programme reads out 2029
microdosing for 'metabolic health' via gray-market telehealth
research-peptide retatrutide used by gym and 'recomposition' communities before and after approval
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: Retatrutide: BLA filed Jan 2027, approved Feb 2028 (13 months after filing, priority review), launched Apr 2028. It delivers ~28–29% mean loss at 80 weeks, up to ~30% in BMI ≥35; the 'surgical-grade loss from a pen' driver is realised here. Its label carries dysesthesia and a slow titration schedule. CagriSema was approved Dec 2026 with modest uptake, because it does not beat tirzepatide. Amycretin is in phase 3, with filing expected 2029; it is not on the US market. Survodutide: phase 3 readouts done, filing expected 2029. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not on the market. Semaglutide's smoking-cessation sNDA was approved Sep 2028 on two phase 3 trials (continuous abstinence weeks 9–24 roughly doubled vs placebo; effect similar to varenicline, better tolerated in people with obesity). The global incretin market is ~$115B (2028). Novo is losing share to Lilly and to ex-US generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Worse with retatrutide's top doses and with uncontrolled gray-market titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; incidence higher in early retatrutide real-world use.
No causal confirmation in long RCTs; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation consolidated in an MDL, no verdicts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concern sharpened by retatrutide's ~30% losses in older adults. Several 2027–28 cohort abstracts associate long-term use in women over 60 with lower bone density.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label recommends resistance exercise and protein counselling; no class warning.
EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.
Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still unquantified, and less discussed in 2028 than in 2026. The addiction indications frame reduced craving as therapeutic, and the complaint is now voiced mainly by anti-pharma and body-liberation groups, so mainstream clinicians treat it as advocacy. No trial includes a validated anhedonia scale as an endpoint.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. The smoking-cessation label lists neuropsychiatric monitoring as standard, not as a specific warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Coverage-driven stops (job change, employer drop, Medicare lockout) are now the commonest cause of discontinuation. Real-world regain lands between the trial and claims figures, at roughly half of lost weight within a year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; it underpins the adherence conditions in Medicare and Medicaid.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More reports at retatrutide-level intake reduction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; professional societies recommend baseline and annual labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The first ≥5-year signal (below) has appeared. Cycling effects are still unstudied, even though ~31% of ever-users have cycled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; FDA Sentinel cycling study commissioned 2028.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~4,000 by mid-2028. Research-peptide retatrutide accounts for a growing share (dosing errors, endotoxin contamination, tachycardia).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised Sep 2027; import alerts on Indian API shippers; personal-importation enforcement mostly unpursued.

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Danish–Swedish registry study (Jun 2028): about 140k long-term users, mostly with type 2 diabetes since the liraglutide and early semaglutide years. Hazard ratio ~1.5 for smell-test-confirmed hyposmia after ≥5 years of continuous use vs SGLT2 users, and no excess before year 4. Estimated absolute excess ~2–3 per 1,000 person-years. Recovery is partial at 12 months off-drug in a subsample. The mechanism is plausible (GLP-1 receptors in the olfactory bulb) but unproven, and confounding by diabetes duration has not been excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC signal review opened Jul 2028; FDA reviewing Sentinel data; no label change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide phase 3 trials, mostly mild, and dose-related.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~28% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~3–4% from 2026 and sugary drinks ~3%. Protein, fibre and 'small-format' SKUs are the main areas of growth. Big CPG firms (e.g. Conagra, Nestlé) run 'companion' lines and are buying protein brands. Firms with heavy exposure to private-label snacks are shedding plants in the Midwest.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down a further ~4% over two years, with heavy-drinker decline as the named driver. Beer is flat-to-down. Non-alc and low-ABV are growing but do not replace lost value. Tobacco is a new adjacent casualty: the Sep 2028 semaglutide cessation label leads Altria and PMI to add 'incretin adoption' to their risk factors.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat. Average ticket is held up by premium small plates. Chains run 'half-portion' menus nationally. Buffets and all-you-can-eat formats are closing locations. Fast-casual bowls with protein add-ons are the winners.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking, with store closures at Torrid and DXL. The body-liberation revival gives inclusive-sizing marketing a small cultural bump but no recovery in volume. Mainstream retailers see re-buying in smaller sizes and fast return cycles from people regaining weight.

fitness.state: Strength-training studios and 'muscle-preservation' programmes are growing, some with telehealth GLP-1 bundles. Big-box cardio gyms are flat. Gray-market peptide sales are spreading through gym communities.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 44%. Coverage is concentrated on diabetes and cardiac codes, a two-tier system. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers attach a BMI or adherence premium differential to wellness programmes (ACA allows up to 30%). Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~8% as plans exclude obesity-only use. Medicare and Medicaid absorb older and poorer users at $245.

pharma.state: Lilly is dominant (tirzepatide, Foundayo, retatrutide). Novo cut US prices and costs, and saw ex-US volume shift to generics. Revenue is growing on volume despite per-unit erosion. Gray-market API from India and China is a reputational and legal fight.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: In affluent suburbs, thinness after 40 is read as being on a drug, as health maintenance. Retatrutide-scale loss is visible and sometimes remarked on as 'reta face'. A larger body now signals either a deliberate refusal or a coverage gap, and people strain to tell which.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers are hardening. Insured professionals and diabetics on covered codes sit at the top; the cash middle class pays $199–299; the lower-income uninsured or dropped use gray-market imports at $60–120 or go without. On-drug rates run 23% in the top income third and 12% in the bottom. BMI premium surcharges fall mostly on hourly workers at large self-funded employers.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Half portions, protein first, and skipping dessert are normal in GLP-1 households. Holiday and church potluck culture has visibly split, with on-drug and off-drug tables. Mennonite, evangelical and Black church food traditions have become sites of open pride in eating.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On it / off it' appears on some dating-app profiles in New York and LA. Couples where one partner lost coverage describe mismatched appetites, around food and otherwise. Low libido is mentioned anecdotally and rarely attributed to the drug.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of every kind, now including nicotine, is officially treatable. The counter-movement is local and loud: fat-liberation organisers in Atlanta and Oakland, a 'Made Whole' evangelical fasting-and-food movement in Texas and Oklahoma, and MAHA-aligned 'natural body' influencers. Each recasts appetite as something God-given, natural or political rather than pathological. Their positions agree on rejection but contradict each other on almost everything else.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: No measurement exists; no trial, registry or label tracks it. It is recognised less than in 2026 because two things absorbed it. The smoking and alcohol results make reduced craving the selling point, and the complaint migrated to anti-pharma and body-liberation spaces, where mainstream medicine discounts it as ideology. Individual users rarely name it; they describe 'growing up' or 'calming down'.
interior_life.framing: Treatment and character. Quieter wanting is described as maturity, recovery or discipline, not as a drug effect.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers report anecdotally that GLP-1-using staff are steady and low-drama; HR wellness vendors cite lower smoke breaks. Sales and hospitality managers occasionally complain about 'flat' closers. Nobody connects either observation to the drug in writing.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Bowling leagues, bar trivia and late-night gaming groups report thinning middle-aged membership, attributed to cost and alcohol trends. Music writers note a vogue for intense, loud, high-sensation live formats. Some musicians openly credit the drug with sobriety and say nothing about the rest.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Anecdotal reports of lower desire and of feeling 'content' rather than 'in love'. Couples therapists in private practice discuss it on podcasts. It does not appear in clinical literature.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable effect on participation. 'Ozempic personality' talk appears as a rhetorical weapon in the body-politics fight ('they're sedating the workforce'), which keeps the effect from being studied neutrally.

state.regulatory_posture: Split. The FDA is fast on approvals (retatrutide on priority review; semaglutide cessation label) and tough on 503B compounders. It is passive on personal importation and research peptides, which it lacks the staff to police. The MAHA wing of the administration publicly criticises 'lifelong drugs for kids' while the same administration markets TrumpRx prices.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Price-controlled public access is in place: the Medicare Continuity Model and Medicaid at $245, plus TrumpRx cash prices. Public obesity coverage depends on proving adherence and response.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare obesity coverage and seven Medicaid waivers require ≥80% refill adherence (pharmacy claims) and documented ≥5% loss at 6 months, with a 12-month lockout on lapse. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers use health-contingent wellness programmes: a BMI ≥30 surcharge (typically $50–100/month) is waived on biometric proof of BMI <30 or on adherence to an approved programme. Adherence is verified by refill data or, increasingly, connected-pen apps synced to wellness vendors. Texas barred BMI surcharges in state-regulated plans (2027), but ERISA self-funded plans are exempt.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army and Air Force issue accession waivers for recruits who reach body-composition standards on a GLP-1, provided they can show ≥6 months off-drug weight stability. TRICARE covers obesity use only for active duty, under strict criteria.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US–India price gap (~$199 vs ~$15) now runs through the gray market. Indian API exporters face FDA import alerts. Canada's generic semaglutide is quietly bought by US border-state residents. Lilly and Novo trade US price concessions for tariff relief.

events.event: Business Group on Health survey: employer weight-management coverage falls to 52%, with another round of large employers limiting GLP-1s to diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes; by 2028 the figure is 44%.

Thousands march in Atlanta and Austin under 'Bodies Aren't Billing Codes' banners; Texas passes a law barring BMI-based premium surcharges in state-regulated plans, which leaves most large self-funded employers untouched.

CMS replaces the expiring Medicare GLP-1 Bridge with a Continuity Model at $245/$50, adding refill-adherence and 6-month response requirements and a 12-month lockout for lapses; seven state Medicaid programmes adopt matching waivers.

FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, about 29% average weight loss, 13 months after filing; it launches in April at $399/month cash, while 'research peptide' retatrutide already sells online for $150–250 and the FDA counts some 4,000 adverse-event reports tied to unapproved incretins.
Danish–Swedish registry study links five or more years of continuous GLP-1 use to a 1.5-fold risk of acquired loss of smell, only partly reversible; EMA opens a signal review the following month.
FDA approves semaglutide for smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in adults with overweight or obesity, the first addiction indication for an incretin drug.

open_tensions: The two-tier access system is now formal. Employer retreat, public adherence lockouts and $60 gray-market imports mean a person's payer, not their physiology, decides whether they are treated continuously or cycle. Nobody knows what years of forced cycling do.

The first ≥5-year signal (hyposmia) has arrived, and the longest-exposed cohort is diabetics who had no alternative. The adolescents starting now will cross the five-year mark around 2031–33, when US generics arrive and use broadens again.

Adherence-conditioned benefits and BMI surcharges now feed refill and connected-pen data to payers and employers. The backlash wants them banned, and the administration both funds the drug and courts the backlash.

Reward blunting has dropped out of view just as the drug is licensed to suppress nicotine craving and is heading toward an alcohol indication. The therapeutic use of the mechanism is crowding out any neutral measurement of its costs.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, with oral initial doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) at $149/month.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
Medicare pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay for covered obesity use, the rate set in the Nov 2025 deals.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.

prose.headline: Pay, Prove It, or Import It: Inside America's Two-Tier Thinness, Where 47 Million Are On and Your Employer Is Watching the Pen
prose.world_in_600_words:
By late 2028 nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about 47 million people, and about 16 million more have been on one and stopped. The drug has become ordinary. The question is no longer whether it works but who pays, and on what conditions.

The answer is plain from the payer mix. If a person has type 2 diabetes, heart disease or sleep apnea, insurance still pays, because the codes protect them. If they have only obesity, their employer probably stopped paying sometime in the last two years: weight-management coverage has fallen from six in ten employers to just over four. The middle class buys brand semaglutide through TrumpRx at $199 a month, Zepbound at about $250, or one of the daily pills at $149. Those who can't manage that use telehealth services that ship Indian generics through a personal-importation loophole the FDA has never had the staff to close, at $60 to $120. Some, mostly younger men from gym culture, inject 'research peptide' retatrutide bought from websites that say it is not for human consumption.

The real retatrutide arrived in April. Lilly's triple agonist takes off nearly 30 percent of body weight in its trials, the kind of loss that used to require bariatric surgery, and costs $399 a month in cash. The surgeons are worried. The fitness industry has rebranded itself around keeping muscle while losing everything else.

Public coverage has become a contract. Medicare's obesity pilot expired and was replaced in January by a model that pays the same $245 but checks pharmacy refills and weigh-ins: miss too many refills, or fail to lose five percent in six months, and coverage lapses for a year. Seven Medicaid states copied it. Large self-funded employers, which never wanted to pay for the drug, found they could legally charge a premium surcharge for a high BMI and waive it if the connected pen reports adherence. Warehouse workers in Ohio pay the surcharge more often than lawyers in Boston do.

The counter-movement is real and splintered. Fat-liberation organisers in Atlanta and Oakland march beside, though not with, evangelical 'Made Whole' congregations in Texas and wellness influencers who distrust pharma on principle. Texas banned BMI surcharges in the plans it regulates, which left the big self-funded employers untouched. The administration that cut the price deals now has a faction that denounces 'lifelong drugs for kids', while child prescriptions keep inching up in wealthy zip codes.

In September the FDA approved semaglutide for quitting smoking and vaping. Combined with the alcohol trials, that settled the drug's public meaning: it quiets wanting, and quieting wanting is treatment. The 2026 stories about people who felt flat on the drug have faded. Nobody measures it, and the people still saying it are the people medicine has learned not to listen to.

In June a Danish–Swedish registry gave the first warning that only time could produce. Diabetics on these drugs for more than five years lose their sense of smell about half again as often as comparable patients, and only partly recover. The absolute risk is small, the mechanism plausible, and the confounders unresolved. Europe opened a review. America's adolescent users, whose five-year mark comes around the time US generics arrive in 2031, are not yet in anyone's dataset.

Snack volumes are down a few points and spirits more. Buffets are closing, half-portion menus have spread nationally, tobacco companies have added the drug to their risk disclosures, and plus-size retailers keep shuttering stores. Nothing has collapsed. The country is lighter, more sober, more monitored and more divided by payer than by anything else.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Ray Delgado wakes at 5:10 in Grove City, Ohio, and the coffee is already made. Denise set the timer. He pours it and holds the mug under his nose out of habit.

Thursday is pen day. He pinches his stomach, clicks, and waits for the little chime as the app syncs. The screen says ADHERENCE 96% — SURCHARGE WAIVED. Ozempic, since 2021, for the sugar. Covered. He doesn't think about it.

Denise's comes in a padded envelope from a pharmacy in Gujarat by way of a website in Delaware, $79 a month. Her job dropped weight coverage last spring. She keeps it in the butter drawer.

At dispatch he routes eleven HVAC calls before nine. Kyle from the warehouse stands at the loading dock with an unlit cigarette, turning it over. 'Doc put me on the shot for these,' Kyle says. 'I just don't care about it anymore.' He puts it back in the pack.

Lunch is half a turkey sub. Ray wraps the other half for tomorrow, which is what he does now.

Tanya in billing hands round a flyer for a church supper, a Made Whole thing, real food, no apologies. Ray says maybe.

Bowling league is Thursday nights. His ball has been in the trunk since March. He drives past the lanes and goes home.

Denise is frying peppers and onions. 'Smells good, right?' she says.

'Yeah,' he says, and leans in close to the pan. He nods anyway.
